Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government data exchange systems. 25 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Integration of CRVS data (births, deaths, marriages) into data exchange for real-time verification and service eligibility
Comments: Prior to the X-Road procurement, Djibouti conducted a pilot on sharing and exchanging information related to childbirth. This pilot was successful but temporary. X-Road was procured to formalize this and more inter-governmental bridges. CRVS integration was the first use case for X-Road. Partially integrated in backend.
revision_notes: Original sources (ega.ee, d4daccess.eu) confirm a 2021 pilot on childbirth data exchange followed by X-Road implementation, but do not establish operational CRVS integration. The World Bank's June 2025 ICR for the Public Administration Modernization Project (P162904) lists the Population Register as one of only 10 systems technically connected to the X-Road interoperability platform at project closing, but explicitly finds that connected administrations 'do not use it or share information with other connected public entities' and continue to exchange data bilaterally and manually. This is closer to under-development/technically-connected-but-non-functional than genuine partial integration, so the score is revised down from 4 to 3.
revised_comments: The Population Register is one of ten government systems technically connected to Djibouti's X-Road-based interoperability platform, following an earlier (2021) pilot on exchanging childbirth data. However, a June 2025 World Bank evaluation finds that connected administrations do not yet use the platform to exchange information with one another, continuing instead to share civil registration and vital statistics data through bilateral, non-automated channels. CRVS integration into the data exchange is therefore best characterised as under development rather than functioning in practice.

Definition: Integration of learner records, academic credentials, enrollment data, and scholarship/bursary systems
Comments: Education digitalization mentioned in the Digital Transformation Strategy. No specific documentation of education registry integration with X-Road. University of Djibouti Espace Creatif digital training launched 2019. Under planning.
revision_notes: Original sources establish only that education digitalisation is mentioned in the Digital Transformation Strategy, with no confirmed registry development. Global Partnership for Education reporting (Jan 2024, updated March 2025) confirms MENFOP is actively developing a digital Education Management Information System (EMIS) with a unique student identification number to track learners, funded through a GPE system transformation grant. This is active development work, not integration with the cross-government X-Road platform (education is not among the 10 systems connected per the 2025 World Bank ICR), so the score is revised up from 2 (Planned) to 3 (Under development), reflecting live EMIS development rather than integration with the national data exchange.
revised_comments: Djibouti's Ministry of National Education and Vocational Training (MENFOP) is developing a digital Education Management Information System (EMIS), including a unique student identification number to track learners' progress through their school career, supported by a Global Partnership for Education system transformation grant. This work remains under development and is not yet linked to the national X-Road interoperability platform, which as of 2025 connects ten government systems but does not include an education registry.

Definition: Integration of health records, patient registration, immunization data, and health insurance into data exchange
Comments: Digitization of healthcare is listed as a key action in the Digital Transformation Strategy 2022 (e-health systems). PAMAP project includes health as a sector for digital services. The World Bank supports e-health development. Under development per strategy but no confirmed X-Road connection for health data yet.
revision_notes: Original sources establish only a strategic intent to digitise health via the 2022 Digital Transformation Strategy, without evidence of implementation. Confirmed newer evidence: DHIS2 rolled out for routine facility-level health data since c.2019-2020 (levels 1-2, with hospital-level integration still in progress); IGAD/MoH launched SORMAS for digital disease surveillance in 2023; and CAMME completed a nationwide rollout of mSupply for pharmaceutical stock and traceability management in April 2025 under the World Bank-financed Health System Strengthening Project. None of these systems are confirmed as connected to the government's X-Road interoperability platform (health is not among the 10 connected systems in the 2025 World Bank ICR). The score of 3 (Under development) is confirmed, reflecting genuine but siloed health-sector digitisation not yet integrated into the cross-government data exchange.
revised_comments: Djibouti's health sector is digitising through several parallel initiatives: DHIS2 for routine health information at primary and regional facility levels, SORMAS for digital disease surveillance (launched with IGAD in 2023), and mSupply for pharmaceutical stock management, completed nationwide in April 2025 under the World Bank-financed Health System Strengthening Project. These systems are not yet connected to the government's X-Road-based interoperability platform, so health system integration into the cross-government data exchange remains under development.

Definition: Integration of court records, case management systems, correctional services data, legal aid information
Comments: Digitization of justice is explicitly listed as a key action in the Digital Transformation Strategy 2022 pillar on digital administration. The GovStack eCabinet use case improves inter-ministerial collaboration. Under development per strategy.
revision_notes: Original sources cited justice digitisation as a listed action in the 2022 Digital Transformation Strategy and the GovStack eCabinet showcase; however, eCabinet addresses inter-ministerial collaboration on decrees and appointments rather than court records or case management specifically, and no independent evidence of justice-sector digitisation implementation was found. The World Bank's June 2025 ICR for the Public Administration Modernization Project lists the ten systems connected to the X-Road interoperability platform (population register, social registry, customs, prefecture, disability register, CSC, telecom, DMONEY, etc.) and justice is not among them. Absent confirmed development activity beyond the strategic mention, the score is revised down from 3 (Under development) to 2 (Planned).
revised_comments: Digitisation of the justice system is identified as a planned action under Djibouti's 2022 Digital Transformation Strategy, within the digital administration pillar. However, justice is not among the ten government systems connected to the X-Road interoperability platform as of the 2025 World Bank project completion review, and no independent evidence of court records or case management digitisation was identified. Justice system integration into the data exchange therefore remains at the planning stage.

Definition: Integration of tax administration and revenue collection systems data into the exchange platform
Comments: E-Tax system (e-filing) implemented 2019, increased compliance 15%. New tax administration system is 'under implementation' as part of the planned integrated financial management system linked to X-Road. ASYCUDAWorld customs operational. Tax systems are standalone but integration into X-Road is planned. Under development phase.
revision_notes: Original sources confirmed e-Tax filing (2019) and ASYCUDAWorld customs (operational, and confirmed as one of the World Bank's 10 systems connected to the X-Road platform per the 2025 ICR), with the core tax administration system described as pending integration. A follow-on World Bank project document (2024) confirms that integration of a new Integrated Tax Administration System (ITAS) and ASYCUDA into the X-Road interoperability platform, alongside other public financial management systems, is an explicit forthcoming activity rather than completed. The score of 3 (Under development) is confirmed.
revised_comments: Djibouti's customs system (ASYCUDAWorld) is one of the ten government systems technically connected to the X-Road interoperability platform, and e-filing for certain taxes has been available since 2019. However, the core tax administration system is being replaced by a new Integrated Tax Administration System (ITAS), whose integration with X-Road and other public financial management systems is planned under a follow-on World Bank-financed project rather than completed. Tax and revenue integration into the data exchange therefore remains under development.

Definition: Integration of social assistance programs, grant registries, beneficiary management systems
Comments: Social protection digitalization is mentioned in Vision 2035 and the Digital Transformation Strategy. No documented integration of social assistance registries with X-Road. World Bank CPF includes human development components but no specifics on social protection data exchange.
revision_notes: Original sources found only a strategic mention of social protection digitalisation with no documented registry integration. The World Bank's June 2025 ICR/IEG review of the Public Administration Modernization Project identifies the Social Registry and the Information System for the Management of Collections and Social Benefits as two of the ten government systems technically connected to the X-Road interoperability platform. WFP/MASS reporting (2024-2025) confirms active expansion and biometric strengthening of the national social registry, now covering c.42-45% of the population. Given the social registry and benefits management system are explicitly named among the platform's connected systems, the score is revised up from 2 (Planned) to 4 (Partially integrated), though the ICR notes actual cross-agency data use via the platform remains limited.
revised_comments: Djibouti's national Social Registry and its Information System for the Management of Collections and Social Benefits are among the ten government systems technically connected to the X-Road interoperability platform, alongside ongoing WFP-supported expansion of the social registry's biometric coverage (reaching approximately 42-45% of the population by 2024-2025). Cross-agency use of the platform for automated data exchange remains limited in practice, but social protection systems are partially integrated into the government's data exchange architecture.

Definition: Whether a formal strategy or policy document exists specifically for government data exchange and interoperability
Comments: Digital Transformation Strategy (April 2022) developed by Ministry of Digital Economy and Innovation (MENI), structured around four pillars including 'Digital Administration (e-government).' Strategy includes: digital identity systems, interoperability platforms, zero paper policy, e-Procurement. Aligned with Vision 2035. GovStack developed national Digital Government Roadmap. SSI 2014-2024 ICT roadmap preceded this.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Djibouti's April 2022 Digital Transformation Strategy, led by the Ministry of Digital Economy and Innovation (MDENI/MENI), remains the comprehensive strategic framework covering interoperability and data exchange. This has since been reinforced by the enactment of Djibouti's comprehensive Digital Code (July 2025), the first in East Africa, and by GovStack's digital government roadmap support. The score of 4 (Comprehensive Strategy Exists) is confirmed.
revised_comments: Djibouti's Digital Transformation Strategy (April 2022), developed by the Ministry of Digital Economy and Innovation, sets out a comprehensive framework structured around four pillars including digital administration and interoperability, aligned with Vision 2035. This strategic framework has since been reinforced by the adoption, in July 2025, of a comprehensive Digital Code covering data protection, cybersecurity and digital services, making Djibouti the first country in East Africa to enact such legislation.

Definition: Extent to which provincial/state and local governments participate in the data exchange
Comments: Djibouti is a small country (approx. 1M population) with a centralized government. High-speed internet in 15 out of 16 ministry/agency sites in the capital only. No documented sub-national government participation in the X-Road data exchange platform. Digital divide between Djibouti City and rural areas documented.
revision_notes: Confirmed. The 2025 World Bank ICR notes an 'Integrated Prefecture System' among the ten systems connected to X-Road, but this refers to the Djibouti-Ville prefecture specifically (the ICR discusses management changes 'in the prefecture of Djibouti-Ville' affecting the Citizen Service Center pilot), not broader sub-national or regional government participation. No evidence was found of participation by Djibouti's other regions (Ali Sabieh, Dikhil, Tadjourah, Obock, Arta) in the data exchange. The score of 1 (National level only) is confirmed.
revised_comments: Djibouti's data exchange platform connects national-level administrations and, within the capital, an integrated prefecture system for Djibouti-Ville, but there is no evidence of participation by the country's other regional or local governments. Given Djibouti's small, highly centralised government structure and the concentration of digital infrastructure in the capital, sub-national participation in the data exchange remains at the national level only.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government data exchange systems. 25 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether data exchange infrastructure and services reach rural and remote areas or concentrate in urban centers
Comments: Persistent digital divide between Djibouti City and rural areas. High-speed internet only in 15 of 16 ministerial sites in the capital. Digital services primarily concentrated in urban areas. Rural infrastructure limitations documented as challenge in CSM Tech analysis. Digital Transformation Strategy acknowledges need to bridge divide.
revision_notes: Confirmed. The 2025 World Bank ICR shows continued concentration of digital government infrastructure (data centre, interoperability platform, Citizen Service Centre pilots) in Djibouti-Ville, with the government only beginning to plan a gradual rollout of 11 Citizen Service Centres nationwide. This corroborates the CSM Tech analysis of a persistent urban-rural digital divide. The score of 1 (Primarily urban) is confirmed.
revised_comments: Government digital infrastructure and data exchange services in Djibouti remain concentrated in Djibouti-Ville, where the national data centre, interoperability platform and pilot Citizen Service Centre are located. A planned rollout of eleven Citizen Service Centres nationwide, including five within the capital, is only beginning, and rural connectivity and service access continue to lag behind the capital. Data exchange infrastructure and services are therefore still primarily urban.
